mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing conversion of clopidogrel to its active thiol metabolite.
effect: Reduced antiplatelet effect has been described; the clopidogrel label advises avoiding concomitant omeprazole or esomeprazole.
management: A prescriber or pharmacist should review the antiplatelet regimen and acid-suppression choice before any change is made.

mechanism: Paroxetine is a potent CYP2D6 inhibitor; metoprolol is primarily cleared by CYP2D6.
effect: Increased metoprolol exposure may cause bradycardia, fatigue, dizziness, or hypotension.
management: Review the combination with the prescriber or pharmacist; heart rate and symptoms may need clinical monitoring.

mechanism: Clarithromycin strongly inhibits CYP3A4, the major enzyme metabolizing simvastatin.
effect: Markedly increased simvastatin exposure and risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis.
management: The combination is contraindicated in simvastatin labeling. A prescriber should choose an alternative antibiotic or statin strategy.

mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and can increase atorvastatin exposure.
effect: Increased risk of statin-associated muscle symptoms and rare rhabdomyolysis.
management: A prescriber or pharmacist should review the combination and consider alternatives or monitoring.

mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9, the main enzyme metabolizing S-warfarin.
effect: Increased warfarin exposure and bleeding risk; INR may rise.
management: Anticoagulation management must involve the prescribing clinician and INR monitoring; no self-adjustment.

mechanism: Omeprazole may inhibit CYP2C19-mediated metabolism of R-warfarin and has been associated with small INR increases.
effect: Modest increase in anticoagulant effect is possible; the magnitude varies.
management: Clinician review and INR monitoring if the combination is started or stopped.

mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, reducing tacrolimus clearance.
effect: Substantially increased tacrolimus exposure with risk of nephrotoxicity and other toxicity.
management: Transplant-specialist review with therapeutic drug monitoring is required.

mechanism: Rifampin induces drug-metabolizing enzymes, which may reduce metoprolol exposure.
effect: Reduced beta-blocking effect is possible; clinical significance varies.
management: Prescriber review and monitoring of heart rate and blood pressure if rifampin is started or stopped.

mechanism: Rifampin induces CYP3A4 and hepatic uptake transporters, altering atorvastatin exposure.
effect: Net effect on atorvastatin exposure can be variable; efficacy may be reduced.
management: Clinician or pharmacist review of lipid therapy during rifampin treatment.

mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP3A4 and can increase simvastatin exposure.
effect: Increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
management: Prescriber or pharmacist review before co-administration; an alternative may be considered.

mechanism: Rifampin induces CYP2C9 and other pathways, increasing warfarin clearance.
effect: Reduced anticoagulant effect and increased thrombotic risk can occur; the effect persists after rifampin is stopped.
management: Anticoagulation specialist review with close INR monitoring during and after rifampin.

mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C19 and may reduce clopidogrel activation.
effect: Potentially reduced antiplatelet effect; evidence is less definitive than for omeprazole.
management: Clinician or pharmacist review of antiplatelet therapy and antifungal choice.
